verdict: Pfizer's revenue was flat at $16.6B because its COVID products kept shrinking — Paxlovid fell 63% and Comirnaty 30% — but the rest of the business grew 7% operationally, Eliquis jumped 25%, and Pfizer raised its full-year guidance.

segments.name: Product revenues
segments.note: Medicines Pfizer sells itself — down 5% as COVID products Paxlovid and Comirnaty shrank faster than other drugs grew.

segments.name: Alliance revenues
segments.note: Pfizer's share of products sold with partners — led by Eliquis, the blood thinner co-promoted with Bristol Myers Squibb, up 25% to $2.5B.

segments.name: Royalty revenues
segments.note: Royalties on products sold by other companies under Pfizer licenses.

opex.name: Selling, informational & administrative
opex.note: Selling, informing doctors and running the company.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new medicines — up 18% as the pipeline expanded.

opex.name: Acquired in-process R&D
opex.note: Research bought from other companies and expensed at once — mostly a one-time $650M charge for the Innovent Biologics licensing deal.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Spreading the cost of drug rights bought in past acquisitions over their useful lives — a non-cash charge.

opex.name: Restructuring & acquisition costs
opex.note: Charges from Pfizer's cost-cutting program and acquisition-related costs.

opex.name: Other deductions, net
opex.note: Costs and losses outside the main operating lines, net of other income.

otherDetail: $10M of profit belonged to noncontrolling interests, partly offset by $1M from discontinued operations and $1M of rounding in Pfizer's millions-rounded lines — a net $8M.
follow100Note: Pfizer kept $19.55 of every $100 of revenue as profit for its shareholders. Rows are rounded to cents.

takeaways.title: Eliquis and cancer drugs are carrying growth
takeaways.text: Eliquis revenue rose 25% to $2.5B and oncology rose 10% to $4.3B, led by Padcev (+55%) and Lorbrena (+44%). Launched and acquired products grew 32% operationally.

takeaways.title: COVID is still shrinking
takeaways.text: Paxlovid fell 63% to $449M and Comirnaty fell 30% to $808M. Excluding both COVID products, Pfizer's revenue grew 7% operationally — the flat headline hides a growing core.

takeaways.title: Guidance went up
takeaways.text: Pfizer raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $1.5B at the midpoint to $62.0–$64.0B and narrowed adjusted EPS guidance to $2.95–$3.05, citing strong year-to-date performance.

oneTimers: $669M of acquired in-process R&D charges, including a one-time $650M charge for the in-licensing and collaboration agreement with Innovent Biologics — worth about $0.10 per share. Pfizer is buying pipeline and expensing it immediately.

$791M of restructuring charges and certain acquisition-related costs, up from $286M a year ago. Together with $1,128M of intangible amortization, these are the main reason GAAP EPS ($0.56) sits well below adjusted EPS ($0.87).
footerNote: Pfizer's printed lines round $1M apart; this chart uses a $3,384M pre-tax profit so the flow balances to the reported $3,242M net income.
